artworks.title: Las Hilanderas (The Fable of Arachne)
artworks.description: Velázquez's Prado masterpiece folds the weaving contest into a tapestry workshop — Athena's challenge and Arachne's pride as Baroque art about art itself.

artworks.title: Pallas and Arachne
artworks.description: Rubens paints Athena's fury as Arachne's loom is struck — the mortal weaver's victory met by the goddess who will turn her into a spider.

artworks.title: Minerva and Arachne
artworks.description: Houasse's Versailles canvas from the Story of Minerva cycle: the goddess confronts Arachne at her loom — Ovid's contest as court allegory of skill and hubris.

popCulture.title: Las Hilanderas
popCulture.creator: Diego Velázquez
popCulture.description: Velázquez's Prado canvas is the modern West's defining image of the Arachne contest — Athena's wrath as meta-painting.

popCulture.title: Arachne
popCulture.description: The weaving contest with Athena remains the myth of artistic pride — a tapestry of divine scandals, then eight legs.
